question.text: Transgastric endoscopic splenectomy: is it possible?
question.context: We have previously reported the feasibility of diagnostic and therapeutic peritoneoscopy including liver biopsy, gastrojejunostomy, and tubal ligation by an oral transgastric approach. We present results of per-oral transgastric splenectomy in a porcine model. The goal of this study was to determine the technical feasibility of per-oral transgastric splenectomy using a flexible endoscope. We performed acute experiments on 50-kg pigs. All animals were fed liquids for 3 days prior to procedure. The procedures were performed under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation. The flexible endoscope was passed per orally into the stomach and puncture of the gastric wall was performed with a needle knife. The puncture was extended to create a 1.5-cm incision using a pull-type sphincterotome, and a double-channel endoscope was advanced into the peritoneal cavity. The peritoneal cavity was insufflated with air through the endoscope. The spleen was visualized. The splenic vessels were ligated with endoscopic loops and clips, and then mesentery was dissected using electrocautery. Endoscopic splenectomy was performed on six pigs. There were no complications during gastric incision and entrance into the peritoneal cavity. Visualization of the spleen and other intraperitoneal organs was very good. Ligation of the splenic vessels and mobilization of the spleen were achieved using commercially available devices and endoscopic accessories.

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The clinical case describes a successful per-oral transgastric splenectomy in a porcine model. The study details the procedure, including gastric incision, entry into the peritoneal cavity, splenic vessel ligation, and spleen mobilization, all performed endoscopically. The absence of complications during the procedure supports the feasibility of this approach.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: The study reports successful endoscopic splenectomy in six pigs with no complications during gastric incision and entry into the peritoneal cavity.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While the case focuses on splenectomy, other abdominal procedures could potentially be performed via this route. However, the primary focus and successful completion of splenectomy in the porcine model strongly suggest the feasibility of this approach for splenectomy.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates successful transgastric endoscopic splenectomy in pigs using a flexible endoscope, with no complications during the procedure. The authors achieved visualization of the spleen, ligation of splenic vessels, and mobilization of the spleen using endoscopic tools. This suggests the technical feasibility of the procedure.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: Successful splenectomy in 6 pigs with no complications and complete mobilization of the spleen using endoscopic techniques
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: While human transgastric splenectomy would require further validation, the porcine model provides strong preliminary evidence supporting the feasibility of this approach

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The case describes a successful porcine model of per-oral transgastric splenectomy with no complications and use of standard endoscopic tools, demonstrating technical feasibility. The procedure was performed under controlled conditions with clear visualization and effective vessel ligation and splenic mobilization.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: Endoscopic splenectomy was performed on six pigs with no complications and successful visualization, ligation, and mobilization of the spleen using commercially available devices.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: No alternative procedures or diagnoses were presented; the focus was solely on feasibility, and the evidence directly supports the possibility of transgastric splenectomy.
